optimizedCVData.summary: Educator and trainer with 8 years in the classroom, specialising in breaking down complex material for diverse audiences and designing structured learning programs that produce measurable outcomes. Raised Year 11 attainment by 15 percentage points over three years by building a data-tracking system, presenting progress reports to senior leadership each term, and redesigning the practical curriculum used by 12 colleagues. Comfortable managing communication across a wide range of stakeholders simultaneously, from students and parents to department heads, and experienced in facilitating both group sessions and individual coaching. Actively building skills in data analysis and Python to support a move into a customer education or onboarding role.

experience.position: Teacher of Physics and Head of Year 9
bullets: Designed and delivered physics instruction to 140 students a year across Years 9 to 13, adapting content and communication style to different ability levels and learning needs.

Raised the share of Year 11 students reaching grade 5 or above from 71% to 86% over three years by tracking individual progress in spreadsheets, identifying at-risk students early and adjusting support plans.

Wrote the department's Year 9 practical curriculum from scratch and trained 12 colleagues to deliver it, producing supporting materials and running hands-on facilitation sessions to ensure consistent implementation.

Managed all parent communication for a year group of 210 students, including weekly calls and two parents' evenings per term, tailoring messaging to different levels of familiarity with educational data and presenting progress summaries to senior leadership each term.
Taught KS3 and KS4 science across multiple year groups, planning and delivering lessons that met varied curriculum requirements and student needs.
Founded and ran the school robotics club, coaching a group of students through project-based learning and introducing them to basic programming and engineering concepts.
Developed differentiated learning materials to support students across a wide attainment range, building skills in content design that translate directly to enablement resource development.
Mentor a group of children aged 9 to 12 in Scratch and introductory Python during evening sessions, structuring each session around clear learning goals and adapting explanations in real time.
Independently learning Python for data analysis using pandas, applying new skills to personal projects alongside formal coursework.
Completed the Python for Everybody certificate on Coursera and currently working through the Google Data Analytics Certificate, demonstrating consistent self-directed upskilling.

coverLetter:
Daniel Okafor
Leeds, UK
daniel.okafor@example.org
+44 20 5550 0188

October 12, 2026

Hiring Manager
Figma

Dear Hiring Manager,

Onboarding a high volume of customers and keeping each one moving toward a clear outcome is, at its core, a curriculum design problem: you need structured content, scalable delivery and a way to measure whether people are actually getting there. That is exactly what I have spent eight years building in a classroom, where I teach physics to around 140 students a year, design the practical curriculum colleagues use across the department, and track progress in spreadsheets I present to senior leadership each term.

The transferable thread between teaching and Figma's scale onboarding programs is tighter than it might first appear. Developing content and enablement resources for different audiences, communicating clearly across varying levels of prior knowledge, and using outcome data to identify where a program needs to change: these are the daily mechanics of running a year group of 210 students and a department curriculum, and they map directly to what this role asks for. I trained 12 colleagues to deliver a curriculum I wrote from scratch, which required the same blend of facilitation, written materials and follow-up that a scalable customer onboarding program depends on. Figma's stated value of "Grow as you go" also reflects how I work: I picked up Python independently and I am mid-way through a Google Data Analytics certificate, because understanding data is how I make better decisions about what a program is and isn't doing.

I would welcome a conversation about how this background fits the team's plans for expanding scale onboarding internationally, and I am available at your convenience.

Kind regards,
Daniel Okafor
